sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year, from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
FY2019 is the one break: operating income fell 58.9% to $5.49 billion and operating margin dropped 11.9pp to 8.1% [D97][F13][D109][F23].
The drop reflects a $6.8 billion goodwill impairment on Shave Care, which the filing ties to currency devaluations, slower category growth and tougher competition [X109][P62].
Operating income then rose 186.2% to $15.7 billion in FY2020, and $8.3 billion of that rise was the absence of the prior-year impairment charge [D148][F14][P71].
US revenue grew from $27.3 billion in FY2018 to $41.7 billion in FY2026, lifting its share of revenue from 40.8% to 47.9% [S10][S18][D512][D534].
In FY2026 revenue rose 3.3%, with Non-US adding 3.1pp and the US only 0.1pp, and the filing credits foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1% [D457][D511][D536][P26].
Fabric & Home Care is the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue and added 0.8pp, on 1% foreign exchange and 1% pricing with unit volume unchanged [D541][D543][P12].
Operating income fell 3.4% against revenue growth of 3.3%, an incremental margin of -25.6%, because gross margin declined and marketing spending rose [D458][D457][D481][P25].
Diluted shares fell from 2,740.4 million to 2,422.5 million, so diluted EPS compounded at 1.9% against 0.5% for net income [X115][X124][F205][F203].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sits above the 22.1% window median and below the 24.3% high and 8.1% low [F30][D648][D647][D646].
The 1.6pp FY2026 decline came from cost of revenue (-1.0pp) and SG&A (-0.6pp), which the filing attributes to lower gross margin and more marketing spending [D470][D483][D485][P25].

Net income still rose 0.5% because other income reached $1.08 billion from $154 million, helped by the Glad joint venture dissolution gain and the absence of the prior-year Argentina charge [D459][X108][X107][P24].
The 22.7% margin ranks at the 80th percentile of five staples peers, whose median is 14.3% [F30][D668][D669].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income, while free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x against a window median of 1.02x [F80][D444][F100][D445][D660].
Working capital added only $29 million: inventory consumed $641 million on safety stock and new products, while payables supplied $919 million [P3].
Capex rose 16.9% to $4.41 billion, 5.1% of revenue and 1.40x D&A, which held free cash flow margin at 17.4% against a 17.2% median [D464][F90][D440][D446][D441][D654].
The filings cited do not explain why capex stepped up in FY2026.
Net cash was -$24.2 billion in FY2026, an improvement from -$24.9 billion in FY2025 [D450][D399].
Net cash of -27.8% of revenue ranks at the 33rd percentile of six staples peers, whose median is -1.0% [D451][D676][D677].
Buybacks of $5.03 billion and dividends of $10.2 billion together equalled 100.7% of free cash flow [X134][X144][D453].
Diluted share count fell 1.3% in FY2026 [D476].
The current ratio was 0.68x in FY2026, below 1.0x, and has never exceeded the window high of 0.88x [F180][R1][D662].
Current liabilities of $38.7 billion exceed current assets of $26.2 billion, and current debt rose to $6.46 billion from $5.38 billion [F160][F150][X194][X193].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in two years, at 116.6% in FY2025 and 100.7% in FY2026 [R2][D402][D453].
Inventory days reached 69 in FY2026 from 52 in FY2017, and inventory grew 8.2% against revenue growth of 3.3% on safety stock and new products [D455][D21][D480][D457][P3].
Operating margin below the 22.1% window median, against 22.7% in FY2026, would confirm that gross margin and marketing pressure is persisting; the test comes in the FY2027 10-K [D648][F30].

Buybacks plus dividends above 100.7% of free cash flow again would confirm a payout running ahead of cash generation, while a return toward the FY2024 level of 86.6% would reverse it; see the FY2027 10-K [D453][D350].

Inventory days above 69, the FY2026 level, would confirm a continuing inventory build and weaker conversion, while a fall toward the FY2025 level of 67 would reverse it; see the FY2027 10-K [D455][D404].
